title: Throwing a Ball on the Moon
learningObjectives: Describe that a ball thrown on the Moon has no air drag and follows ballistic flight.
Explain that horizontal speed stays constant while vertical motion slows at rate g.
Use ymax = V0^2 / (2*g) to predict the maximum height of a throw.

sources.title: Throwing a ball on the Moon (project-authored test text)
sources.attribution: Written by the Make knowledge interactive project team for testing.

evidence.quote: On the Moon there is no air, so a thrown ball feels no drag at all.

explanations.text: On the Moon a thrown ball feels no drag and its flight is purely ballistic.

evidence.quote: Nothing pushes the ball sideways, so the horizontal speed stays U0 for the whole flight

explanations.text: With no sideways push, horizontal speed stays U0 while the ball moves across the ground.

evidence.quote: On the Moon g is about 1.62 m/s^2, roughly one sixth of the 9.8 m/s^2 we feel on Earth.
Putting that time into the height equation gives the highest point: ymax = V0^2 / (2 * g).

explanations.text: Moon gravity is about 1.62 m/s^2, so the highest point follows ymax = V0^2 / (2 * g).

predictions.prompt: A ball is thrown on the Moon with g = 1.62 m/s^2, horizontal speed 8 m/s and vertical speed 6 m/s. Predict the maximum height.
The same throw with horizontal speed 8 m/s and vertical speed 6 m/s is made with Earth gravity 9.8 m/s^2. Predict the maximum height.
A ball is thrown on the Moon with horizontal speed 10 m/s and vertical speed 10 m/s. Predict the maximum height.
